recommended_assay.test_name: Retrieve the 2026-06 FAP imaging read and, if it is uninformative, quantitative FAPI PET uptake in known metastatic nodes

therapeutic_implication.notes: Enrolls FAP-positive solid tumors and would require imaging-confirmed uptake in the target lesions.

rationale: FAP here is an imaging-research lead, not a treatment lead: the one FAPI PET on record found no FAP-avid urothelial disease and lit up granulomatous prostate tissue instead. The 2026-06 repeat study is worth retrieving because it has already been done, but a stromal signal on multiplex immunofluorescence will not qualify anyone for a radioligand protocol. Recent SBRT to the nodal disease adds treatment-related fibroblast activation, which makes any new uptake harder to attribute.

relevance_rationale: MAGE-A4 carries the first approved TCR-T therapy and the patient is HLA-A*02:01 positive, so he cleared the HLA gate for that class. Expression testing in 2024 answered the other half.
status_evidence: profile.json:biomarkers[8] MAGE-A4 tumor expression negative (2024-06), confirmation_status 'confirmed'
profile.json:biomarkers[8] testing was performed as part of screening for a MAGE-A4 TCR trial for which the patient was HLA-matched

therapeutic_implication.approval_status: FDA approved for MAGE-A4-positive HLA-A*02 synovial sarcoma
therapeutic_implication.notes: Closed here by the negative expression result rather than by tumor type.
Also closed by the negative expression result.

rationale: MAGE-A4 was tested on tumor tissue and was negative, which forecloses the MAGE-A4 TCR-T class despite the matching HLA type. The row is kept because it is the case's own worked example of why an HLA match is not an option until expression is measured, which is exactly the state PRAME and NY-ESO-1 are in now. Nothing further is needed unless a new specimen is ever sequenced and shows re-expression.
notes: Cancer/testis antigen expression is heterogeneous within a tumor, so a negative on one specimen is not a permanent statement about every lesion. It is enough to close trial screening today.

relevance_rationale: Without an HLA class I type, every HLA-presented target in the panel is unassessable rather than negative. This patient has allele-level typing on file and is HLA-A*02:01 positive, which is the restriction most current TCR-T and ImmTAC products name.
status_evidence: profile.json:biomarkers[12] HLA-A*02:01 positive, high-resolution class I and II typing 2025-01, confirmation_status 'confirmed'
profile.json:biomarkers[12] full typing withheld from the derived profile as quasi-identifying, which does not affect the A*02:01 call

therapeutic_implication.approval_status: Product-specific; each names its restricting allele
therapeutic_implication.notes: The A*02:01 result satisfies the restriction for the PRAME and NY-ESO-1 programs in this survey; expression is the remaining gate for each.

rationale: Allele-level typing is already on file and positive for A*02:01, so the prerequisite that would otherwise make the whole intracellular-antigen class unassessable is satisfied. That is what lets the PRAME and NY-ESO-1 rows stand as expression questions instead of HLA questions. The full typing is held in the local record and should be supplied directly to any protocol that needs the class II alleles.
notes: Loss of heterozygosity at the HLA locus in the tumor is a separate escape mechanism from germline genotype and is not addressed by this result.

recommended_assay.turnaround_estimate: 1-2 weeks, and the assay is not routinely offered

therapeutic_implication.approval_status: Not approved and not in active development
therapeutic_implication.notes: MMAE payload, which the established neuropathy argues against in any case.

rationale: SLITRK6 is genuinely urothelial-restricted but the only binder that reached patients has not advanced past phase 1, so a positive stain would open nothing that is currently enrolling. With one block left and several higher-yield stains competing for it, this is the wrong slide to spend. Revisit if a SLITRK6 program reopens.

relevance_rationale: PSCA is upregulated in bladder cancer as well as in prostate and pancreatic cancer, and this patient also carries a treated prostate primary. No PSCA result exists.
status_evidence: absent from profile.json:biomarkers[]; no PSCA result on file
not part of the 2026-08 research MXIF panel recorded in profile.json

therapeutic_implication.notes: Enrolling in castration-resistant prostate cancer rather than urothelial carcinoma.

rationale: PSCA is plausibly expressed in this tumor but the clinical bench is confined to early prostate and pancreatic CAR-T protocols, none of which is enrolling urothelial patients. Normal prostate, bladder and pancreas expression is also an on-target risk that matters more than usual in a man with a prostate primary and prior pancreatitis. Test only if a PSCA protocol opens to this disease.

therapeutic_implication.notes: Developed in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer; the prostate primary here is in remission with undetectable ctDNA, so it does not create an entry point.

rationale: STEAP1 programs are running in castration-resistant prostate cancer, and this patient's prostate primary has no evidence of disease, so neither his urothelial disease nor his prostate history gives him a route to one, and some normal urothelial expression complicates the tumor-versus-normal argument on top of that. There is nothing to order here today.

relevance_rationale: EPHB4 is overexpressed on bladder and prostate cancers with a tumor-vascular component, which puts it in scope by tumor type. Its clinical bench is one fusion protein that has not advanced.
status_evidence: absent from profile.json:biomarkers[]; no EPHB4 result on file
not part of the 2026-08 research MXIF panel recorded in profile.json

therapeutic_implication.notes: Studied in Kaposi sarcoma, head and neck cancer and mesothelioma, not in urothelial carcinoma.

rationale: EPHB4 earns a line on a bladder gap list and nothing more: the evidence tier is preclinical, the one clinical-stage binder was studied in other diseases, and endothelial expression makes the therapeutic window uncertain. Spending scarce tissue on it would displace stains with real options behind them.

relevance_rationale: ITGA3 is upregulated on bladder carcinoma and drives invasion, so the panel puts it in scope for this tumor type. There is no anti-ITGA3 binder in clinical development.
status_evidence: absent from profile.json:biomarkers[]; no ITGA3 result on file

rationale: ITGA3 has no clinical-stage binder, so a result either way would change nothing that can be acted on today. The row exists so the reader can see the target was considered and set aside, not because a stain is worth ordering. Broad normal epithelial expression would also limit any future window.
